purpose: Two original learner-facing instructional scripts for the B02 Foundation Book II canonical Labs; private grading and review remain separate.
provenance: FICTIONAL market examples only. No claims of historical order book observations, licensed market data, executed trades or verified vendor latency.

labs.title: Premarket Information Release and Repricing
labs.objective: At a declared decision pause, separate a document's processing or acceptance timestamp from verified public availability, delivered evidence and later market activity.

definitions.explain: For a U.S.-listed stock, trading activity before the regular 9:30 a.m. Eastern Time opening session. Actual eligible hours depend on broker, venue and security.
A timestamp showing when a filing entered an official processing system. It is not automatically proof the filing was already publicly accessible or reached the learner's data feed.
The earliest time for which reliable evidence establishes that the document was accessible to the public. This must be verified independently of acceptance when the distinction matters.
The declared pause at which the learner must make a decision using only evidence then available. Later timestamps are outside that information set.
A change in displayed quotes or traded prices. Coincidence with an information release alone does not establish that the release caused the change.

nineStageJourney.teach: Talia: We will act as investigators, not hindsight traders. Our job is to decide what could have been known at a specific time. Every time in this exercise is fictional.
nineStageJourney.learnerAction: Read the event ledger and state the decision cutoff before making a claim.

nineStageJourney.teach: A filing may have an acceptance timestamp, a later verified public-access time, and still later delivery to a particular news feed. Those are three different events. A quote may update later still. Market evidence must be timestamped, sourced, and available by the pause. A post-pause update cannot be smuggled into an earlier decision.
nineStageJourney.learnerAction: Explain the difference between acceptance, public accessibility, delivery and subsequent quote movement.

nineStageJourney.teach: FICTIONAL event ledger (ET): 08:04:00 filing accepted; 08:06:00 public availability independently verified; 08:07:20 learner's information screen records delivery; 08:08:00 decision pause; 08:09:00 displayed bid/ask move. There is no recorded trade or size at the pause.
nineStageJourney.learnerAction: Sort the four different event categories and mark which precede the declared pause.

nineStageJourney.teach: At 08:08, the quote movement scheduled for 08:09 is still unknown. Talia asks for a decision without telling you how the later quotes will move.
nineStageJourney.learnerAction: Record the claim you can support at 08:08 and one claim you must not make yet, before seeing the post-pause event.
nineStageJourney.feedback: If you use the 08:09 quote to justify an 08:08 forecast, your evidence set includes future information. Rebuild it using the cutoff.

nineStageJourney.teach: Talia: Verify every clock. An observation is the documented event. A hypothesis is a possible explanation. A trade decision also needs spread, order-size and eligibility information that this ledger lacks.
nineStageJourney.learnerAction: Classify: (a) verified document availability before 08:08, (b) later quote change, (c) an assertion that the filing caused a fill, (d) a defensible no-trade decision.
nineStageJourney.feedback: An absence of order-book or transaction evidence is not an invitation to assume a fill. Choose 'not enough evidence' when appropriate.

nineStageJourney.teach: Ungraded authoring draft. Official grading can become available only after a private rubric receives individual authenticated Owner review. Do not award mastery based on this lesson alone.
nineStageJourney.learnerAction: In your own words, describe the available evidence, the unknowns and a justified no-trade condition at the cutoff.

nineStageJourney.teach: Talia: Correct your chronology before you correct your conviction. A later market move may be consistent with a hypothesis without proving that hypothesis or confirming you could have traded it.
nineStageJourney.learnerAction: Explain any earlier use of information not available by the pause and revise the observation.
nineStageJourney.feedback: When confused, write two columns labeled 'available at cutoff' and 'learned later'.

nineStageJourney.teach: Independent FICTIONAL case: filing accepted 08:04, public access verified 08:12, first vendor delivery 08:14, learner paused at 08:08 and later saw a quote at 08:16.
nineStageJourney.learnerAction: Apply the same chronology rule to this new sequence. Do not borrow the first scenario's times.
nineStageJourney.feedback: The independently verified access/delivery times belong after the pause. Never infer earlier access from an acceptance timestamp alone.

nineStageJourney.teach: Your learning record should capture the decision cutoff, specific source evidence, hypothesis limits and revised reasoning—not a fabricated trading return.
nineStageJourney.learnerAction: Save the learning reflection through the existing authorized progress workflow when implemented; do not claim a server save without confirmation.

dataIntegrity: No hindsight use of post-cutoff quotes
Do not equate SEC acceptance with verified public availability
No causal assertion from temporal correlation
No execution claim without order eligibility, spread, size and actual fill evidence
editorialChecks: Verify public-versus-acceptance terminology against SEC documentation
Ensure the independent transfer is not the same sequence
Screen-reader chronology table uses actual labels
Check all nine stages retain user input before reveal

labs.title: Bid, Ask, Last, Spread, and Midpoint in a Frequently Updating Quote
labs.topic: Quote mechanics and asynchronous last prints
labs.objective: Calculate a snapshot's quoted spread and mathematical midpoint while separating last-traded price, bid/ask timestamps, quoted size and actual execution evidence.

definitions.explain: The displayed highest price a buying participant is currently quoting under the observed market-data convention. It may change or disappear; size and market access matter.
The displayed lowest price a selling participant is currently quoting under the observed market-data convention. It does not guarantee a specific order will fill.
The price of the most recent reported transaction in the selected feed. Its timestamp need not match the current quote timestamp, and it is not a standing executable offer.
Best displayed ask minus best displayed bid for one synchronized snapshot: spread = ask - bid.
The arithmetic average of the displayed best bid and ask: midpoint = (bid + ask) / 2. It is a reference calculation, not a guaranteed fill price.

nineStageJourney.teach: Talia: We will read the quote, not guess the next candle. Prices and timestamps in this case are invented and are not a real brokerage quote.
nineStageJourney.learnerAction: Before calculating anything, identify which fields are standing quotes and which describe a completed reported trade.

nineStageJourney.teach: When a valid bid is $10.00 and ask is $10.08, the displayed spread is $10.08 - $10.00 = $0.08. The midpoint is ($10.00 + $10.08) / 2 = $10.04. A last reported trade at $10.12 can differ because it may have been reported earlier, from a different condition or from another moment; a mismatch alone is not proof of a data error.
nineStageJourney.learnerAction: Explain each of the three numbers and which two determine the spread and midpoint.

nineStageJourney.teach: FICTIONAL snapshot: bid $10.00 at 09:45:10 ET, quoted size 100 shares; ask $10.08 at 09:45:10, quoted size 75 shares; last reported print $10.12 timestamped 09:45:07. No order submission or fill was observed.
nineStageJourney.learnerAction: Calculate the current displayed spread and midpoint. Describe the last print separately, including its earlier timestamp.

nineStageJourney.teach: Talia: At this snapshot a learner considers buying 250 shares. The displayed ask size is only 75 shares. Do not assume the quoted ask can fill the entire proposed order.
nineStageJourney.learnerAction: Record what you expect to know and what you cannot know about a hypothetical 250-share buy before any future quote or execution event is revealed.
nineStageJourney.feedback: The current top-of-book quote is not a promise of execution across a larger incoming order.

nineStageJourney.teach: A quote update changes the fictional best bid to $10.03 while the ask remains $10.08 at the new synchronized snapshot. The last print remains $10.12 with its original time.
nineStageJourney.learnerAction: Recalculate the updated spread and midpoint, then identify what did not change.
nineStageJourney.feedback: At the new synchronized snapshot spread = $0.05, midpoint = $10.055; whether a platform rounds the displayed midpoint to cents is a display choice, not evidence of a fill.

nineStageJourney.teach: Ungraded authoring draft. Grading and mastery require a separately authenticated, reviewed private assessment version.
nineStageJourney.learnerAction: Describe why the three quoted/printed prices cannot be interchanged when estimating current transaction risk.

nineStageJourney.teach: Talia: A quoted spread is one possible source of execution friction. Slippage, depth, hidden liquidity, routing and order type can matter. A stale last price is not today's executable bid or ask.
nineStageJourney.learnerAction: Explain a previous calculation, state its timestamp, and name one missing piece of order-execution evidence.
nineStageJourney.feedback: If your calculation used last instead of bid or ask, identify the correct inputs and retry.

nineStageJourney.teach: Independent FICTIONAL quote: synchronized bid $24.90 size 50 shares; ask $25.10 size 40 shares; last print $25.35 timestamped three seconds earlier; hypothetical buy order for 100 shares.
nineStageJourney.learnerAction: Calculate the new displayed spread and midpoint, then explain why 100 shares cannot be guaranteed at the displayed ask.
nineStageJourney.feedback: The new spread is $0.20 and midpoint $25.00. The displayed ask size is smaller than the proposed order; even matching size would not guarantee a fill.

nineStageJourney.teach: A sound outcome is a correct price calculation plus a precise statement of what the snapshot does not show. Do not convert a hypothetical quote observation into a claim that a trade occurred.
nineStageJourney.learnerAction: Record the observation and its limits in the existing member Journal workflow when authorized; verify save confirmation before claiming persistence.

dataIntegrity: Snapshot bid and ask timestamps must be comparable
Spread and midpoint derive from bid and ask, never last
Do not silently round subcent midpoint in calculation
Historical trade print is not a firm order quote
Size 75 cannot guarantee a 250-share buy at that price
editorialChecks: Use accessible labels for bid, ask, last and sizes
Verify independent transfer does not reuse first quote
